models_evaluated: guideline screening rules (three, including age-limited rule)
BRFSS self-reported-diagnosis model with positive-unlabeled correction

links.outcome: Sensitivity for HbA1c-defined undiagnosed diabetes, EBM versus guideline rules at equal referral rate
links.effect: At the USPSTF referral rate (44% of adults), the EBM found 85% (95% CI 75-94) of undiagnosed cases versus 65% (55-74) for the age-limited rule.
links.quote: At the US Preventive Services Task Force referral rate (44 % of adults), the 13-item EBM found 85 % (95 % CI 75-94) of HbA1c-defined undiagnosed cases versus 65 % (55-74) for the age-limited rule.

links.outcome: Share of model attribution carried by access and socioeconomic items under self-reported versus HbA1c label
links.effect: Access and socioeconomic items carried 23.8% of attribution under the self-reported label and 17.7% under the HbA1c label.
links.quote: Access and socioeconomic items carried 23.8 % of attribution under the self-reported label and 17.7 % under the HbA1c label.

links.outcome: Whether self-reported diagnosis training labels encode access-to-care bias
links.effect: Self-reported diagnosis labels partly encode access to care; positive-unlabeled correction raised BRFSS model AUROC from 0.775 to 0.816.
links.quote: Self-reported diagnosis labels partly encode access to care.

links.outcome: External-cohort discrimination and calibration of measurement-only EBM
links.effect: In the external cohort (388 adults), the measurement-only EBM reached AUROC 0.788 but needed recalibration.
links.quote: externally, a measurement-only EBM reached 0.788 but needed recalibration.

unlisted_practices: Correcting self-reported-label bias using a diagnosis-propensity model and positive-unlabeled learning
Anchoring the training label to a laboratory measurement (HbA1c) rather than self-report
Offline on-device deployment of an interpretable model with reproducibility check of predictions

screen.reason: The study evaluates the impact of training label bias (self-reported vs. biomarker-anchored) and explicitly tests a positive-unlabeled learning correction to mitigate healthcare-access bias in screening models.
